newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest direct hogs seen steady-up $0.50 -trade.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest direct hogs seen steady-up $0.50 -trade.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices Friday were seen steady to $0.50 per cwt higher, lifted by continued strong packer demand, livestock dealers said.
Hog prices also were seen underpinned by outlooks for light hog movement Friday as producers have become current, they said.

Lighter average hog weights reflected the increased current status, sources said. Iowa/southern Minnesota barrow and gilt weights averaged 253.1 lbs the week ended last Friday, down from 254.1 lbs the previous week, USDA said on Wednesday.
USDA also estimated overall U.S. slaughter hog weights last week at 256 lbs, the same as the previous week but up slightly from the actual average weight of 255 lbs a year earlier.
Several buyers in Illinois and Indiana said hog movement also was curtailed by increased fieldwork as producers prepare for spring planting.

Cash hog prices also were seen underpinned by demand from packers who were closed on Monday for Easter. Some of those plants will be running a shift Saturday in attempts to recover some of the production lost over the holiday, dealers said.

Interior Iowa/southern Minnesota top hog prices delivered to plants were seen ranging from $51.00 to $51.50, dealers and packer buyers there said. Illinois hogs at the plant were seen trading at $51.50 to $52.00.
Indiana/Ohio top prices at plants were projected at $51.00 to $51.50, sources there said.
